notes: SCOPE: this fragment is the HIGH-VOLTAGE half of the Ethernet interface (IEEE 802.3af/at PD electrical + the 37-57 V domain). The 10/100 data half (TX/RX pairs, W5500, magnetics data side) is a sibling fragment. Full derivation with a source per number: boards/lumina-carrier/research/interface-poe-48v.md.

DELIBERATE OMISSION - MERGE TRAP: 'high_speed' and 'diff_pairs' are OMITTED, not empty. Per reference/constraints_schema.md an EXPLICIT empty diff_pairs list DISABLES check_diffpair entirely, and a naive dict-merge of an empty list would clobber the Ethernet fragment's pairs. Absent keys no-op cleanly; empty ones do not. Do not 'fix' this by adding empty lists.

NET NAMES ARE PROPOSALS. netlist_audit (P4) raises missing_net at ERROR severity for any voltages[].net absent from the netlist, so all seven names must be reconciled with the sheet plan before P4 or deleted. Names are written bare (power-symbol style like +3V3/GND/VBUS); any that ends up as a local label instead needs a leading '/'. check_creepage itself is tolerant (it skips absent nets), netlist_audit is not.

V48_RTN IS DECLARED -57 V ON PURPOSE. check_creepage compares declared voltages pairwise and treats unlisted nets as 0 V. Board GND is the SWITCHED negative (hot-swap FET drain); the TPS2378 recommended operating conditions specify that node as 0 to 57 V ABOVE the raw negative (VSS), so the raw negative sits up to 57 V BELOW board GND. Declaring -57 makes the checker demand 0.60 mm between the raw negative and GND - the FET drain-source spacing, the detection/classification network and the bridge negative. Declaring 0 would silently skip all of it. Side effect: V48_RAW-to-V48_RTN reads as 114 V, which gives the same 0.60 mm outer and 0.20 mm (not 0.10 mm) inner - conservative and still below the fab minimum.

THE BINDING SPACING NUMBER: 0.60 mm on outer layers (F.Cu/B.Cu), 0.10 mm on inner layers, between the 48 V domain and every other net. IPC-2221B Table 6-1 column B2 (external, uncoated, sea level to 3050 m), 51-100 V band; the 31-50 V band gives the same 0.60 mm, so 48 V and 57 V do not differ. Corroborated by TI's own PD layout note (0.025 in = 0.635 mm between VSS and VDD). Inner 0.10 mm is below JLC's 0.127 mm fab minimum, so inner layers get it for free; the 0.60 mm on outer layers is ~4x the fab minimum and will NOT happen by accident.

DO NOT CLAIM THE COATED COLUMN. IPC-2221B B4 (permanent polymer coating) would allow 0.13 mm, but soldermask over a narrow gap is not a qualified void-free coating, and decisively: check_creepage.py implements only B2 and B1. A layout designed to 0.13 mm will FAIL the P8 gate with no waiver path short of editing the checker.

SAFETY CLASSIFICATION - plain answer: FUNCTIONAL INSULATION ONLY. 57 V DC is below the IEC 62368-1 ES1 limit of 60 V DC (subclause 5.2.1.1), so no basic/supplementary/reinforced safeguard is required against the 48 V domain for shock protection. IPC-2221 is a reliability/arcing standard and is the governing number; IPC does not separate creepage from clearance at this voltage, so 0.60 mm covers both. No IEC 60664-1 creepage computation is invoked. If a formal 62368-1 assessment is ever needed it is a system-level activity (enclosure, cabling, the PSE's mains isolation), not a board-level one.

WHAT CHANGES IF THE CONVERTER IS NON-ISOLATED (Q5 default, PROVISIONAL): the voltage and the 0.60 mm do NOT change. What changes is that there is no isolation barrier anywhere on the board, so IEEE 802.3's requirement for 1500 Vrms isolation between the MDI leads and ALL accessible external conductors (including frame ground) cannot be met by the DC-DC. Microchip states it directly: with non-isolated designs the end application must provide the isolation. It is then satisfied ONLY by there being no accessible external conductor: non-conductive enclosure, no chassis earth, Ethernet as the only external connection. The Q5 default is the compliance argument, not a convenience.

IF AN ISOLATED FLYBACK IS EVER CHOSEN the on-board barrier spacing is a completely different number: minimum 0.080 in = 2.0 mm on FR4 between traces either side of a 1500 Vrms barrier. Do not confuse 0.6 mm (functional, within one domain) with 2.0 mm (barrier, between two domains).

GROUNDING - direct answer: in a non-isolated PD the 48 V domain and the logic domain SHARE ONE GROUND. Board GND is the PD return, DC-connected through the input bridges to the Ethernet pair conductors; every GND net floats at PoE potential relative to earth. The magjack's 1500 Vrms isolates the cable-side windings from the PHY-side windings, so it protects the W5500's TX/RX pins from the 48 V and from cable common-mode - but PoE power is tapped from the CABLE-side centre taps, so that barrier is bypassed by design for the power path. The magjack protects the PHY from the power, not the board from the cable.

PD ENVELOPE, af (Type 1) build 1: 12.95 W guaranteed at the PD input, 37-57 V input range, 350 mA max DC at the PD, PSE gives 350 mA DC with up to 400 mA peaks, 20 ohm max cable loop, 2-event classification NOT required. at (Type 2) upgrade: 25.50 W, 42.5-57 V, 600 mA DC, PSE 600 mA DC with 686 mA peaks, 12.5 ohm loop, 2-event classification MANDATORY.

D-01 RISK (blocks the 'resistor change only' promise): Type 2 requires the PD to RECOGNISE 2-event classification and assert an AT flag - that is silicon, not a resistor. The requirements' power budget cites Skyworks AN956 / Si3402-B, whose datasheet says it supports IEEE 802.3 Type 1 (Class 3 and below) ONLY. If the Si3402-B is selected, D-01's no-respin upgrade to PoE+ is impossible. Choose a Type 2 capable controller (TI TPS2378 class, Microchip PD70201/PD70211 class) or D-01 is void. P2/P3 decision, but a D-01 conformance question, not a preference.

CLASSIFICATION RESISTOR (the D-01 upgrade lever): Class 3 for build 1 (26-30 mA, 6.49-12.95 W), Class 4 for the upgrade (36-44 mA, 12.95-25.5 W). R_CLASS values are PART SPECIFIC because they absorb the controller's own bias current: Microchip gives 45.3 ohm (class 3) / 30.9 ohm (class 4); TI TPS2378 gives 90.9 ohm / 63.4 ohm for the same classes. Take the value from the datasheet of the part actually chosen - the two vendors differ by 2x.

DETECTION: PSE probes at 2.80-10.0 V; the PD must present 23.7-26.3 kohm differential resistance and 50-120 nF input capacitance. Standard implementation is a 24.9 kohm 1% detection resistor plus an 82-100 nF / 100 V ceramic across the port. The detection resistor is switched out above ~12.8 V so it may be a low-voltage 0402/0603 part; the capacitor must be 100 V rated. Classification finger is 15.5-20.5 V, mark event 6.3-10.1 V.

MPS (Maintain Power Signature) - a NEGATIVE constraint on firmware: the PD must draw at least 10 mA DC (or a 10 mA pulse of >=75 ms at least once every 325 ms), and the PSE removes port power after roughly 300-400 ms without it. 10 mA at 57 V is 0.57 W; the carrier's own 1.5 W overhead budget is ~26 mA at 57 V, so MPS is satisfied by normal operation and NO dummy load is needed. The rule is: no sleep or standby mode may take total PD input current below 10 mA, or the PSE drops the port and the fixture reboots. (MPS numbers are from secondary sources - the clause text is paywalled - so the design rule is deliberately conservative.)

INRUSH / SEQUENCING: PD inrush is actively limited to <=350 mA (Type 1); real parts limit to 140-240 mA typical. IEEE 802.3 requires an 80 ms inrush-to-operating-state delay, so the carrier's 48 V high-side switch to the daughter must NOT fire before that delay expires. Maximum PD bulk capacitance is a part limit (240 uF for the Microchip family) - oversized bulk both stalls inrush and can trip the PSE.

SURGE / TVS - the mandatory protection element: a 58 V standoff TVS across the rectified PD input (bridge outputs, VPP to the raw negative), at the front end before the PD controller. Microchip names SMBJ58A or equivalent; TI calls a 58 V TVS across the controller's input rails the minimum requirement for ALL surge test levels. Why 58 V: the standoff must sit above the 57 V maximum port voltage so it never conducts normally, and the clamp must stay below the controller's 100 V absolute maximum. Sizing check: the 400 W SMAJ58A clamps at 93.6 V at only 4.3 A - that is 6.4 V of margin to the 100 V abs max, and 4.3 A is BELOW the 4.65 A per-line peak a 1 kV IEC 61000-4-5 class-2 surge delivers into one shorted line. Prefer the 600 W SMBJ58A and confirm its I_PP at P3.

UNEARTHED-PD DIVIDEND: with no earth connection there is no inviting return path for a common-mode surge, so TI's guidance is that the normal front-end filter plus TVS is adequate lightning protection for an unearthed PD. The MOV-to-earth network that an EARTHED PD reference design carries is NOT applicable here and must not be copied. Assumed EMC target: IEC 61000-4-5 installation class 1-2 (500-1000 V all-lines-to-ground) for an indoor basement fixture - no brief states an EMC requirement.

COMPONENT WORKING VOLTAGE, not just spacing: 0402 and 0603 resistors are typically rated 50 V working, 0805 typically 150 V. ANY resistor sitting across the 48 V domain must be 0805 or larger, or split into two in series. This bites bleed/discharge resistors and any 48 V sense divider. Port capacitors must be 100 V rated.

CONVERTER INPUT RATING: CAR-REQ-02 says >=60 V with margin. Recommend >=80 V (100 V preferred). 57 V is only the steady-state maximum; the rail sits behind a TVS that clamps near 93 V and behind a hot-swap FET rated 100 V. A 60 V part has 3 V of margin on a rail whose own controller is rated 100 V. Recommendation, not a re-opening of CAR-REQ-02.

EXPANSION CONNECTOR - RATED VOLTAGE IS A REAL DISQUALIFIER. The connector's rated working voltage must be >=57 V, not >=48 V; prefer >=100 V. Worked example of the trap: the Hirose DF40 0.4 mm mezzanine, an obvious pick for a stacked daughter, is rated 50 V AC/DC and 0.3 A - it fails on both counts. A 2.54 mm dual-row header is 250 V AC/DC, 3 A per contact, 600 V AC withstanding. Read the rated-voltage clause of any candidate; do not assume it.

EXPANSION CONNECTOR - PITCH IS SET BY THE LAND PATTERN, not the connector body. check_creepage measures pads, so each 48 V pad needs >=0.60 mm to every neighbouring pad. Computed gaps (pitch minus pad diameter): 2.54 mm pitch with 1.60 mm pads = 0.94 mm PASS; 2.00 mm with 1.20 mm pads = 0.80 mm PASS; 1.27 mm with 0.80 mm pads = 0.47 mm FAIL (needs pads <=0.67 mm, zero margin); 0.50 mm SMT = 0.20 mm FAIL. RECOMMENDATION: >=2.00 mm pitch for the 48 V pins, 2.54 mm if the pin budget allows. The same clearance applies through the board - a signal passing under a 48 V pin's antipad on another layer is checked too.

EXPANSION CONNECTOR - GUARD PIN: not required by IPC-2221B or IEEE 802.3 (no standard mandates one), but required by failure analysis. The failure mode is 57 V on a 3.3 V logic pin, which destroys the MCU instantly; realistic mechanisms are a solder bridge, debris, flux tracking or a partial mis-seat, none of which CAR-REQ-16 keying prevents. A GND pin adjacent to the 48 V pin converts that fault into a 48 V-to-GND short, which the current-limited high-side switch already has to survive under CAR-REQ-14. An EMPTY position multiplies spacing (0.94 mm becomes 3.48 mm at 2.54 mm pitch). ICD recommendation: 48 V pins at ONE END of the connector, GND on both sides of every 48 V pin, at least one GND pin (plus an empty position if the budget allows) between the 48 V group and the first logic pin, and rails ordered 48 -> 12 -> 3.3 so adjacent pins are never more than one rail step apart. A 2-row header has no first-mate/last-mate control, so the ICD must state that the daughter tolerates 48 V arriving before or after 3.3 V.

EXPANSION CONNECTOR - THE ICD MUST NOT OVER-PROMISE CURRENT. Q6's default asks for 48 V raw 2 A continuous / 3 A capability, but the PoE SOURCE cannot deliver it: 350 mA DC / 400 mA peak (af), 600 mA DC / 686 mA peak (at). Anything above that must come from local capacitance, and the carrier deliberately holds none beyond the PD controller's own bulk. Sustained overdraw trips the PSE and the port drops. Keep a 3 A-rated contact (cheap, big thermal margin) but state BOTH numbers in the ICD, e.g.: '48 V raw: contact rated 3 A; source limited to 0.35 A DC / 0.40 A peak (af build), 0.60 A DC / 0.686 A peak (at upgrade); charging current above this must be governed in firmware.' Otherwise a daughter designer sizes a cap bank against current that can never arrive. This is the hardware half of the average-energy governor.

CAR-REQ-17 second half (every 48 V-tapping daughter carries a bleed path) is a DAUGHTER obligation but belongs in the carrier's frozen ICD text. The carrier must not defeat it: no series diode on the 48 V pin that would strand the daughter's stored charge above the carrier's own bleed path.

PIPELINE GAP (grep-verified): rules_gen.py does NOT read the 'voltages' key, and the net class it emits for power nets carries clearance max(fab_min, 0.2) mm. Nothing therefore makes the P7 router honour 0.60 mm - the violation only surfaces at P8 check_creepage, after routing. At P5, add an explicit HV net class in the .kicad_pro (or a named .kicad_dru clearance rule keyed on A.NetName - per LEARNINGS, the A.Net token silently matches nothing and the LATER rule wins), or plan on a P8-to-P7 rework loop.

PLACEMENT HINT for the merged file (not emitted here): keep the whole 48 V domain - magjack centre taps, both bridges, TVS, PD controller, hot-swap FET, class/detect network, converter input - as one contiguous block at the RJ45 end of the board, with the expansion connector's 48 V pins on the nearest edge of that connector. Every millimetre of 48 V copper that wanders into the logic field is another pair the 0.60 mm rule applies to. A placement 'separation' entry between the PD block and the ESP32-S3/W5500 block also serves the CAR-REQ-18 thermal argument.

OPEN - O-2 (Q5/Q4a interaction, for the architect): Q4a's default puts the LEDs on a separate module on its own heatsink, wired to the daughter. In a non-isolated PD that heatsink and its wiring sit at PoE potential and are plausibly 'accessible external conductors', which IEEE 802.3 requires to be isolated from the MDI. If the LED module is touchable, metal, or shares a heatsink with anything earthed, the non-isolated topology is non-conformant. Needs an explicit answer before P2 commits a converter topology.

OPEN - O-3 (Q9 interaction): the default recovery path is an internal UART/BOOT header. A USB-serial adapter plugged into an earthed laptop IS a second earthed connection to a board floating at PoE potential. Either state in the design doc that the recovery header is used only with PoE disconnected, or specify an isolated USB-UART. Not a board change - an ICD/design-doc line item.
